biomarker_name.evidence_quote: MTX-R exhibited significant decrease in Bacteroidetes. Differentially abundant ASVs included B. thetaiotaomicron, B. uniformis, B. vulgatus. Immune cells included B220+, Foxp3+ CD4+, CD44+ CD69+ CD4+, Gr1+ CD11b+, IFN-γ+ CD4+, IL-17A+ CD4+
biomarker_name.section: Results — Clinical relevance; Results — Post-treatment microbiome decreases host immune activation
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified across different experimental contexts: taxonomic (bacterial taxa), functional (gene families), and immunological (immune cell populations). These are reported at study level as they characterize findings across the cohort.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: fold change percentage. DAS28 score decreased ≥1.8. Immunocyte populations as percentage of cells or fold change percentage normalized to pre-MTX group.
biomarker_unit.section: Methods — Analysis of immune cell markers from transplanted gnotobiotic mice; Results — Clinical relevance
biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type. Taxonomic markers reported as relative abundance or fold change; immune populations as percentage or fold change; clinical response as DAS28 score.

value: Study includes gnotobiotic mouse experiments with human microbiota colonization (5 experiments total)
In vitro bacterial growth studies on 45 isolates from 6 phyla
RNA-seq conducted on 4 bacterial isolates with varying MTX sensitivity
Untargeted metabolomics on 2 isolates (B. theta and C. asparagiforme)
Ex vivo incubation of stool from 30 MTX-naive RA patients
Longitudinal clinical cohort of 23 RA patients (16S-seq) and 17 RA patients (metagenomic sequencing)
RA patient responders defined as DAS28 decrease ≥1.8 with continued MTX use
MTX doses: 1 mg/kg (low) and 50 mg/kg (high) in mice; standard of care doses in patients
DSS inflammatory challenge used in fecal microbiota transplant experiments
Flow cytometry analysis of immune cells from spleen, small intestine, and colon
Correlation analysis between 12 MTX-modulated ASVs and immune cell populations in 20 transplant recipient mice
Metagenomic analysis identified 6,409 differentially abundant gene families (nominal p<0.05) over time
Microbiota transplant experiments used pre- and post-MTX treatment stool samples from 3 responders
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Germ-free mice colonized with human stool. 45 isolates from 6 phyla. RNA-seq on 4 isolates. Metabolomics on 2 isolates. Ex vivo incubation of 30 patients' stool. Longitudinal cohort n=23 (16S) and n=17 (shotgun). DAS28≥1.8 responders. Doses 1 and 50 mg/kg mice; standard care patients. DSS challenge. Flow cytometry spleen/intestine. Correlation analysis 12 ASVs in 20 mice.
uncurated_metadata.section: Abstract; Methods — Experimental Model and Subject Details; Methods — In vitro bacterial growth studies; Results
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive multi-system study design combining in vivo mouse models, in vitro bacterial work, ex vivo patient samples, and clinical cohort data to assess MTX effects on microbiota and immune function.

host_species.evidence_quote: C57BL/6J mice (females, ages 6–16 weeks). RA patients met American College of Rheumatology classification criteria. Stool samples from healthy donor and treatment-naive RA patients.
host_species.section: Methods — Gnotobiotic mouse studies; Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
host_species.notes: Study includes both human subjects (RA patients and healthy control donor) and laboratory mice (C57BL/6J strain, germ-free). Human subjects are the primary clinical focus; mice are experimental models colonized with human microbiota.
